# Calendar runtime injection ownership review

## Conclusion

Static review found no blocker in the two-line ownership fix or the new regression test. Deep-copying the frozen bundle and the optional IA-owned overlay before injection isolates the mutable nested metadata that downstream normalization fills in place. The injection destinations remain the caller-owned `groups`, `modules`, `screens`, and `actions` lists, as intended.

This was a read-only review of the implementation and tests. I did not run tests, Django, a database, generators, or index operations. Root reported that the five new regression cases failed against the immutable `cf44` parent; that RED result was not independently reproduced here.

## Definitions and mutation path

`RuntimeMetadataInjectionBundle` is a frozen dataclass, but its `groups`, `modules`, `screens`, and `actions` fields are tuples of mutable `dict[str, Any]` values (`apps/terminal/infrastructure/tui_metadata_runtime_injection_registry.py:170-179`). Its outer attributes cannot be rebound, but the nested records are mutable. `_canonical_runtime_bundle` returns this same bundle class, and every entry in `RUNTIME_METADATA_INJECTIONS` is created through that function (`:242-260`, `:518-521`). The repository routes every registered entry through `_inject_runtime_bundle` (`apps/terminal/infrastructure/tui_metadata_repository.py:989-999`); I found no separate production bundle class or same-class route bypassing this helper.

The alias path is real: `_append_unique_payloads` only makes a shallow top-level `dict` copy when adding or replacing group/module/screen payloads (`apps/terminal/infrastructure/tui_metadata_repository_helpers.py:10-31`). Action additions and replacements likewise use shallow `dict(...)` copies (`tui_metadata_repository.py:1039-1060`). Nested field dictionaries can therefore still point back into a bundle. `validate_tui_metadata` mutates fields in place by supplying `fields`, `input_type`, `required`, `default`, `placeholder`, `value_type`, and `presentation_semantic` defaults (`apps/terminal/application/tui_metadata.py:167-182`, `:743-757`, `:785-786`). A later validation could consequently write derived keys into a shared declaration.

The `ia_owned_action_copy` is an overlay: the current normalizer constructs it from IA payload actions and, today, copies only `label` and `description` (`tui_metadata_repository.py:480-492`). The injected action merge applies that overlay after the bundle action (`:1039-1040`, `:1058-1059`), so IA-owned values retain precedence. The new test's IA-owned `fields` case is a synthetic nested-overlay case; it exercises the generic `dict[str, dict[str, Any]]` contract even though the current builder does not put fields there.

## Change and behavioral review

The production diff is limited to a clearer docstring and two local copies at the start of `_inject_runtime_bundle` (`tui_metadata_repository.py:1002-1015`): `bundle = copy.deepcopy(bundle)` and `owned_action_copy = copy.deepcopy(ia_owned_action_copy or {})`. `copy` was already imported and used elsewhere in the repository module.

The copies isolate nested records for all four bundle sections and the IA overlay before any shallow append/merge. They do not copy or replace the destination lists, so the method still updates the caller's payload and returns the same inserted/replaced count. The `replace_existing` flag, key-based matching, missing-screen skip, runtime-only `audience`/`effect` merge for non-replacing action collisions, IA overlay precedence, and count increments are unchanged. Deep-copy preserves the equality comparisons used to decide whether a replacement/merge counts as a change.

## Test review and limits

`tests/unit/terminal/test_runtime_injection_input_ownership.py:21-58` covers four combinations: bundle-owned versus IA-overlay-owned nested fields, crossed with insertion versus replacement. It checks that normalization supplies `default`, the reported count is one, and the original bundle and overlay remain structurally equal to deep snapshots. The fifth case (`:61-75`) normalizes the real published graph and compares the complete canonical `RUNTIME_METADATA_INJECTIONS` tuple with a deep snapshot, covering all registered bundle instances and catching any mutation to their nested declarations.

The full-registry assertion is the important same-class coverage: every canonical runtime record has the same frozen bundle type, and the actual published-normalization path exercises the registry as a whole. The synthetic test does not separately assert the emitted `presentation_semantic` value, but its input-equality assertions protect that field from being written back into either owner; the full published-graph equality assertion protects registered declarations. It also does not add a dedicated test for the existing non-replacing action-collision merge branch. That branch's control flow is unchanged by this patch, so I see no need to expand this ownership-focused test for that case.

## Review boundary

No code, tests, generated files, governance files, or Git index were changed by this review. Dynamic behavior and the parent-reported RED remain unverified here by design.

+"""Normalization must not change reusable runtime metadata declarations."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json
+from copy import deepcopy
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Any, Literal
+
+import pytest
+
+from apps.terminal.application.tui_metadata import validate_tui_metadata
+from apps.terminal.infrastructure.tui_metadata_repository import PublishedTuiMetadataRepository
+from apps.terminal.infrastructure.tui_metadata_runtime_injection_registry import (
+    RUNTIME_METADATA_INJECTIONS,
+    RuntimeMetadataInjectionBundle,
+)
+from tests.unit.test_tui_workbench import _metadata_payload
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("replace_existing", [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("field_owner", ["bundle", "ia"])
+def test_normalization_preserves_injection_input_fields(
+    replace_existing: bool,
+    field_owner: Literal["bundle", "ia"],
+) -> None:
+    """Inserted and replaced actions normalize their own fields, from either owner."""
+    action = _metadata_payload()["actions"][0]
+    field = {"key": "exchange", "label": "交易所", "binding": "query", "required": True}
+    owned_copy: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
+    if field_owner == "bundle":
+        action["fields"] = [field]
+    else:
+        owned_copy[action["key"]] = {"fields": [field]}
+    bundle = RuntimeMetadataInjectionBundle(
+        coverage_key="test_owned_fields",
+        actions=(action,),
+        replace_existing=replace_existing,
+    )
+    before_bundle = deepcopy(bundle)
+    before_owned = deepcopy(owned_copy)
+    old_action = deepcopy(action) | {"label": "Old label"}
+    payload = _metadata_payload(actions=[old_action] if replace_existing else [])
+    payload["screens"][0]["default_action_key"] = action["key"]
+
+    injected = PublishedTuiMetadataRepository._inject_runtime_bundle(
+        bundle=bundle,
+        groups=payload["groups"],
+        modules=payload["modules"],
+        screens=payload["screens"],
+        actions=payload["actions"],
+        ia_owned_action_copy=owned_copy,
+    )
+    result = validate_tui_metadata(payload)
+
+    assert injected == 1
+    assert result["actions"][0]["fields"][0]["default"] == ""
+    assert bundle == before_bundle
+    assert owned_copy == before_owned
+
+
+def test_published_normalization_preserves_runtime_declarations() -> None:
+    """The real published graph cannot add derived keys to shared runtime bundles."""
+    before = deepcopy(RUNTIME_METADATA_INJECTIONS)
+    path = (
+        Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
+        / "config/tui/published/tui_operation_graph.published.json"
+    )
+    repository = PublishedTuiMetadataRepository(published_path=path)
+
+    result = repository.validate_and_normalize_runtime_payload(
+        json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
+    )
+
+    assert result["actions"]
+    assert RUNTIME_METADATA_INJECTIONS == before
